newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia beet plantings early but seen below plan.
newsitem.headline: Serbia beet plantings early but seen below plan.

text.p: Favourable weather has allowed Serbian farmers to start sugar beet plantings a week earlier than usual, but the 1997 area is unlikely to reach the government target of 100,000 hectares, industry sources said.

"The sugar beet compaign began over the weekend as both temperature and moisture of the soil are favourable for sowing," Milan Patkovic, an official of the Jugosecer sugar producers association, told Reuters on Monday.
Jugosecer forecast 1997 plantings at 60,000-70,000 ha, well below the official goal.
According to unofficial reports, production deals for beet had been concluded for some 40,000 ha by last Friday.
Farmers are still owed money from the state for the 1996 crops.
The government has promised to clear its 800 million dinars debt to them by March 15, about 425 million dinars of which is for sugar beet.

"Government payments are late and slow and it will effect this year's production," said Ljiljana Vasic, head of the association of agricultural cooperatives of the country's bread-basket of Vojvodina.
The 1996 beet area has been estimated at 70,000 ha.
